source_spans.text: Let X be an arbitrary finite alphabet and let C be a prefix-free code. We prove an upper bound on expected code length as a function of the symbol distribution and derive a corresponding compression-ratio inequality.

The theorem is stated only for abstract codes and distributions. It makes no source-level claim about an agent or adaptive system, relevance-preserving representation, learning, prediction, control, decision, memory, perception, action organization, or any other functional capacity.
